BiblicalUsage: Sheminith is probably an eight-stringed instrument, or a musical direction, and it is named only three times. Once it is played: Mattithiah and Elipheleh and Mikneiah and Obed-edom and Jeiel and Azaziah, with harps on the Sheminith to excel, when the ark was brought up. Twice more it stands in the titles of psalms, the sixth and the twelfth, where the chief musician is told to sing upon Sheminith.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the harps on the Sheminith were part of the joy of bringing the ark home, and the music mattered enough to name its tuning, because God delights in worship done with skill.
